questoes.enunciado: Identify the structure indicated by the double arrows.

alternativas.feedback: Correct. This image shows a two well defined lymphoid nodules located in the lamina propria of a tonsil. The presence of the lighter-staining germinal center indicates that this a secondary nodule.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the region outlined in this image.

alternativas.feedback: Correct. The presence of a germinal center in this solitary lymphoid nodule indicates that this is a secondary nodule.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the tissue outlined in these images.

alternativas.feedback: Correct. Diffuse lymphoid tissue, composed of lymphocytes, is present within the lamina propria or submucosa (as seen here) of many organs, where it filters tissue fluid. During an immune response, recruitment of additional lymphocytes leads to the formation of lymphoid nodules.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the structure outlined in this image.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. The white pulp of the spleen consists of diffuse (T-dependent) and nodular (B-dependent) lymphoid tissues that surround arterioles after they leave trabeculae. The diffuse tissue forms a sleeve around each arteriole. The lymphoid nodules are suspended within the diffuse areas. The surrounding red pulp consists of splenic cords and sinuses.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the cell indicated by the arrows.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. Immunoblasts, which are present within the germinal center, are large lymphocytes with a euchromatic nucleus. Cell division of these cells produces additional lymphocytes, which accumulate around the darker staining periphery of the nodule.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the aggregate of lymphoid tissue that fills the field.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. Tonsils, located in the lamina propria, consist of numerous lymphoid nodules embedded in diffuse lymphoid tissue. The tonsil is surrounded by an incomplete capsule of connective tissue; crypts extend into the tonsil.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the structure indicated by the double arrow.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. Primary lymphoid nodules are clusters of lymphoid cells located as solitary nodules in the lamina propria of tubular organs (as here) and as aggregates in tonsils and Peyer’s patches. A primary lymphoid nodule consist mostly of small lymphocytes aggregated in the lamina propria and filter tissue fluid. The absence of a pale, germinal center distinguishes this primary nodule from a secondary nodule.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the organ that fills the field.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. The lymph node is entirely encapsulated and has lymphoid nodules located only in the cortical region of the organ. Medullary cords and sinuses identify the medullary region.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the structure indicated by the arrows.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. The lymph node is a fully encapsulated organ; the capsule is composed of dense irregular connective tissue.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the region indicated by the double arrow.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. The central region of a lymph node is termed the medulla and contains medullary cords and medullary sinuses. These sinuses receive lymph which has percolated through the cortex.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the structure indicated by the rectangle.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. High endothelial venules are unique blood vessels because their endothelium is a simple cuboidal epithelium rather than the typical simple squamous. This shape allows ready passage of lymphocytes through their walls.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the structure indicated by the arrows.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. Beneath the capsule of the lymph node is the subcapsular sinus, which receives and filters the lymph entering via the afferent lymphatic vessels.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the cell indicated the arrows.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. Macrophages are present among the numerous lymphocytes in the subcapsular sinus of the lymph node. Macrophages can be distinguished by their larger nuclei, the presence of phagocytosed material in their cytoplasm and ruffled cell borders.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the organ that fills the field.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. Like the lymph node, the spleen is entirely encapsulated; however, in the spleen, connective tissue trabeculae extend farther into the organ than do those of the lymph node. In lymph nodes, lymphoid nodules are confined to the cortex; lymphoid nodules in the spleen are present throughout the organ, forming part of the white pulp.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the structure indicated by the arrow.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. The spleen is covered by a thick capsule of dense irregular connective tissue from which long trabeculae penetrate into the parenchyma.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the organ that fills the field.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. Spleen is differentiated from lymph node and thymus because it lacks the cortex and medulla these organs possess. Lymphoid nodules, part of white pulp, are scattered throughout the spleen; their distinguishing feature is their central arteriole, which is displaced toward the margin when a nodule develops within the PALS surrounding the arteriole.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the region that fills the field.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. The red pulp of the spleen is intermixed with the white pulp but appears less compact. The red pulp consists of splenic cords and splenic sinuses, which are filled with blood that has been filtered through the white pulp and the intervening splenic cords.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the organ that fills the field.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. The thymus is an encapsulated organ that lacks lymphoid nodules. The organ has lobules, each of which has a distinct cortex, composed of densely-packed lymphocytes, and a palely stained medulla, containing the distinctive Hassall's corpuscles.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the structure indicated by the double arrow.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. Hassall's corpuscles are located in the medullary regions of the thymus and are composed of deteriorating reticular epithelial cells that form the framework of this organ.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the region outlined in this image.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. The inner region of the lymph node cortex, the paracortex, is a T-dependent area. It lies just beneath the superficial cortex where the lymphoid nodules are located. Beneath the paracortex is the medulla. Under antigenic stimulation, T cells in this region become activated, replicate and leave the lymph node via the efferent lymphatic vessels. These T cells are then returned to the blood and carried to peripheral sites throughout the body.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the cells indicated by the arrows.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. The stromal meshwork supporting the thymus is formed by cells of epithelial, rather than connective tissue, origin and, therefore, are called epithelial reticular cells. The nuclei of these cells are large, spherical and euchromatic.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the cells indicated by the arrows.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. In this germinal center, macrophages (tingible body macrophages) with phagosomes in their cytoplasm, indicate the phagocytic activity occurring in this region. These macrophages are phagocytosing apoptotic cells in various stages of degradation that occurs during immune selection. The term “tangible” refers to the fact that the phagocytosed material is stainable, mostly condensed chromatin fragments.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the structure indicated by arrows.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. This palatine tonsil is covered by the stratified squamous epithelium of the oropharynx that invaginates into the tonsil, forming multiple crypts. A partial capsule of dense connective tissue separates the tonsil from underlying connective tissue. Tonsils form a ring of lymphoid tissue in the lamina propria around oral and nasal pharynges.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the cells indicated by the arrows.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. The splenic sinuses are venous sinuses and hence are lined by endothelial cells. However, these cells are unique, having large nuclei that bulge into the lumen of the sinusoid. Additionally, these cells are extremely long, with their longitudinal axes oriented parallel to the flow of blood in the sinus.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the structure indicated by the arrows.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. The darkly staining perimeter of a secondary nodule is the mantle (corona), composed mainly of tightly packed B lymphocytes formed in the germinal center. After antigenic stimulation, large immunoblasts in the germinal center divide to form B lymphocytes that accumulate in the peripheral mantle.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct.  This image shows a two well defined lymphoid nodules located in the lamina propria of a tonsil.  The presence of the lighter-staining germinal center indicates that this a secondary nodule.
